text:
alice.k: Quick proposal — introduce "quota buckets" as a first-class concept in routing policy. This would let us assign short stable bucket IDs per route and expose them in telemetry and SDKs. Rationale: let the console show per-customer budgeted quotas without exploding metric cardinality. Thoughts?

ben: Slight clarification — per-customer-per-route bucket or a global bucket id per route? Can you sketch the API surface?

alice.k: Per-route per-customer mapping. Sketch of policy object: 

```json
{
  "route": "chat.v1",
  "bucket_id": "bkt-1234",
  "limit_per_min": 120
}
```

We'll emit a short header `X-RD-Quota-Bucket: bkt-1234` on responses and include `quota_bucket` in SDK response meta.

carla: Minor nit on the header name — prefer `x-rd-qbucket` (shorter, matches other headers). Also we need to keep compatibility with existing `x-rd-routehint` telemetry.

samir: SDK impact summary: Py/TS/Go need to surface the bucket id into the response meta and add optional client config `default_quota_bucket` to control client-side preferring behavior. Make it optional so no breaking change.

li: From console POV: if we get stable bucket ids we can show a "bucket-level burn" chart without high-cardinality labels. UX question: do we map bucket_id -> human alias in UI? I think yes.

rachel: Rollout plan idea: enable header + server-side bucket assignment in hosted as a canary for 2 weeks, with telemetry sampling switched on for selected orgs. Dedicated customers can opt-in earlier. We must avoid a massive influx of new series in metrics. @devex-bot can you schedule a canary window?

devex-bot: Scheduled canary job: `quota-buckets-v1` on hosted-route-prod. Window: 2026-06-12T08:00Z -> 2026-06-26T08:00Z. Notifying infra oncall.

carla: On the SDKs, we also need a clear fallback when header absent (old clients / private deploys). Please add doc snippet and keep default behavior unchanged.

samir: Example (py) -- opt-in, non-breaking:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., default_quota_bucket=None)  # opt-in behavior\resp = client.chat.create(...)
# resp.meta.quota_bucket is either server-assigned id or None
print(resp.meta.quota_bucket or client.options.default_quota_bucket)
```

ben: Concern: if integrators can set arbitrary bucket ids we get cardinality again. We should make bucket assignment server-only. If clients ask to prefer a bucket, server can honor or ignore.

alice.k: Strong +1 to server-generated-only bucket ids. Clients may request `prefer_bucket=true` but final id is chosen by server policy.

console-ux: UX note: we'll add a "Quota buckets" page under Billing -> Quotas. Fields: alias, bucket_id, linked routes, owners, burn-rate graph, linked evals. Need `bucket_id->org` mapping in telemetry payload to join with billing. Also: ability to alias bucket (friendly name) and set alerts.

rachel: Action items roundup: @samir open PRs for py/ts/go with opt-in meta field; @carla finalize header name and write server acceptance rules; @console-ux provide wireframes by EOD Thu; infra to prepare metric sampling knobs.

samir: Will open SDK PRs today. Will keep response meta additive and optional to avoid breakages.

alice.k: Thanks all — let's keep this conservative. Plan to sync again after PRs land. :rocket:
